claim: XPD is a Superfamily 2 (SF2) DNA helicase involved in DNA repair and transcription initiation.
source_text: XPD helicase, a Superfamily 2 (SF2) DNA helicase involved in DNA repair and transcription initiation
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about XPD helicase's classification and cellular functions.

claim: Monomeric XPD unwinds duplex DNA in 1-bp steps.
source_text: We show that monomeric XPD unwinds duplex DNA in 1-bp steps
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental measurements using optical tweezers with single base pair resolution as described in the manuscript.

claim: XPD exhibits frequent backsteps during DNA unwinding.
source_text: yet exhibits frequent backsteps
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed in the experimental data showing backward steps during unwinding.

claim: XPD undergoes conformational transitions manifested in 5-bp backward and forward steps.
source_text: undergoes conformational transitions manifested in 5-bp backward and forward steps
evidence_reasoning: The 5-bp steps are observed in the data, and their interpretation as conformational transitions is inferred from the stepping patterns and structural considerations.

claim: Forward, single-base pair stepping of XPD helicase utilizes the spontaneous opening of the duplex.
source_text: we provide the strongest and most direct evidence thus far that forward, single-base pair stepping of a helicase utilizes the spontaneous opening of the duplex
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is drawn from quantifying the sequence dependence of stepping dynamics and correlating it with base pair opening probabilities.

claim: The proposed unwinding mechanism may be a universal feature of DNA helicases that move along DNA phosphodiester backbones.
source_text: The proposed unwinding mechanism may be a universal feature of DNA helicases that move along DNA phosphodiester backbones.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative statement about the generalizability of the findings to other helicases.

claim: SF1 and SF2 helicases contain a conserved motor core comprised of a nucleotide binding site in the cleft between two RecA-like domains.
source_text: The two largest helicase superfamilies, SF1 and SF2, contain a conserved motor core comprised of a nucleotide binding site in the cleft between two RecA-like domains
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge cited from previous literature (Singleton et al., 2007; Fairman-Williams et al., 2010; Beyer et al., 2013; Raney et al., 2013).

claim: SF1 and SF2 helicase domains move as a ratchet-like inchworm, translocating along single-stranded NA by 1 nucleotide during each ATP binding and hydrolysis cycle.
source_text: suggest these domains move as a ratchet-like inchworm, whereby the helicase translocates along single-stranded NA by 1 nucleotide (nt) during each ATP binding and hydrolysis cycle
evidence_reasoning: This mechanism is supported by ensemble kinetic and structural studies cited in the manuscript.

claim: The mechanism of base pair separation by helicases has remained elusive.
source_text: Despite these findings, the mechanism of base pair separation has remained elusive.
evidence_reasoning: This represents the state of knowledge in the field prior to this study.

claim: Previous studies investigating helicase mechanisms have been limited by assumptions on helicase step size, slippage, and backstepping.
source_text: Previous studies investigating this question by varying NA sequence (Cheng et al., 2007; Johnson et al., 2007; Manosas et al., 2010) have been limited, as assumptions on helicase step size, slippage, and backstepping have prevented definitive statements
evidence_reasoning: This is a critical assessment of previous work based on cited literature.

claim: Previous studies have lacked the resolution to assess stepping dynamics directly.
source_text: These studies have lacked the resolution to assess stepping dynamics directly.
evidence_reasoning: This is a statement about the limitations of previous experimental approaches.

claim: Distinguishing between helicase mechanisms requires interrogating helicase activity at the single-protein level with high spatio-temporal resolution.
source_text: Distinguishing between mechanisms requires interrogating helicase activity at the single-protein level, and with high spatio-temporal resolution.
evidence_reasoning: This is a logical inference about the experimental requirements needed to resolve mechanistic questions.

claim: XPD helicase exhibits repetitive, non-processive unwinding bursts.
source_text: Single XPD helicase exhibits repetitive, non-processive unwinding bursts
evidence_reasoning: This behavior is directly observed in the experimental traces shown in Figure 1D.

claim: XPD exhibited repetitive unwinding 'bursts' during which the hairpin gradually unfolded, then suddenly and completely re-annealed.
source_text: the protein exhibited repetitive unwinding 'bursts' during which the hairpin gradually unfolded, then suddenly and completely re-annealed
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct description of the observed experimental behavior.

claim: Re-annealing occurred in large backward jumps of −6.3 ± 1.6 bp.
source_text: While unwinding was gradual, re-annealing occurred in large (−6.3 ± 1.6 bp, mean ± SD; N = 144 bursts) and sudden backward jumps
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental data.

claim: The re-annealing rate was high (>100 bp/s), much faster than the translocation speed of 13 ± 2 nt/s.
source_text: The re-annealing rate was high (>100 bp/s; N = 144 bursts), much faster than the translocation speed of 13 ± 2 nt/s
evidence_reasoning: The re-annealing rate is measured from the data, while the translocation speed is cited from Honda et al., 2009.

claim: The re-annealing is ATP independent.
source_text: ATP independent
evidence_reasoning: This is determined from experimental observations of re-annealing behavior.

claim: The re-annealing observations are inconsistent with helicase translocation on the opposite strand.
source_text: inconsistent with helicase translocation on the opposite strand, as observed in other systems
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference based on comparing the observed behavior to known mechanisms in other systems.

claim: XPD can backslide by several base pairs without dissociating from its DNA substrate.
source_text: These observations suggest a mechanism of repetitive unwinding in which XPD can backslide by several base pairs without dissociating from its DNA substrate.
evidence_reasoning: This mechanism is inferred from the observed repetitive unwinding bursts and re-annealing behavior.

claim: The ARCH domain of XPD can encircle the translocating DNA strand during unwinding.
source_text: Structures and biochemical studies suggest that the ARCH domain of XPD can encircle the translocating DNA strand during unwinding
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by cited structural and biochemical studies (Liu et al., 2008; Wolski et al., 2008; Kuper and Kisker, 2012; Kuper et al., 2012; Pugh et al., 2012).

claim: The ARCH domain provides a potential structural basis for backsliding without dissociation.
source_text: providing a potential structural basis for backsliding without dissociation
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference connecting structural features to the observed backsliding behavior.

claim: XPD's behavior is reminiscent of the 'repetitive shuttling' previously reported for the SF1 helicase Rep.
source_text: Although XPD's behavior is reminiscent of the 'repetitive shuttling' previously reported for the SF1 helicase Rep
evidence_reasoning: This comparison is made to previously reported behavior in Rep helicase (Myong et al., 2005).

claim: Rep helicase shuttling was detected during translocation on ssDNA, not duplex unwinding.
source_text: First, Rep helicase shuttling was detected during translocation on ssDNA, not duplex unwinding.
evidence_reasoning: This is a statement about the known behavior of Rep helicase from previous studies.

claim: Shuttling in Rep is mediated by formation of a transient DNA loop that allows rapid 'snapback' to its initial position on DNA.
source_text: Second, shuttling in Rep is mediated by formation of a transient DNA loop that allows rapid 'snapback' to its initial position on DNA.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the known mechanism of Rep shuttling from previous studies.

claim: The data disfavors a DNA looping mechanism for XPD backsliding because re-annealing usually occurred in multiple jumps rather than a single snapback.
source_text: Our data disfavors such a mechanism, as the re-annealing usually occurred in multiple jumps, rather than a single snapback.
evidence_reasoning: This inference is based on the observed pattern of re-annealing in the experimental data.

claim: Formation of a ∼12-bp loop is unlikely at the applied tension.
source_text: Furthermore, formation of a ∼12-bp loop is unlikely at the applied tension.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference based on understanding of DNA mechanics under tension.

claim: XPD helicase has low processivity, unwinding on average only 12 ± 3 bp per burst.
source_text: The second notable feature is the low processivity of XPD helicase (Figure 1D). Although the full hairpin measured 89 bp, on average only 12 ± 3 bp (mean ± SD; Table 1) were unwound during each burst.
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental data.

claim: No unwinding activity was detected when the helicase loading site was <10 nt.
source_text: No activity was detected when the loading site was <10 nt.
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed in the experiments varying loading site length (Figure 2E).

claim: Processive activity was detected only when the binding site was ≥19 nt, long enough to accommodate two or more XPD helicases.
source_text: Processive activity was detected only when the binding site was ≥19 nt, long enough to accommodate two or more XPD helicases.
evidence_reasoning: The observation is from data, and the interpretation about accommodating multiple helicases is an inference.

claim: The rate 1/τ1 for first unwinding varied linearly with XPD concentration.
source_text: The rate 1/τ1 for first unwinding varied linearly with XPD concentration (black circles, Figure 2H)
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct observation from the titration experiments.

claim: τ1 corresponds to the time for a single XPD protein to bind to the DNA.
source_text: indicating that τ1 corresponds to the time for a single XPD protein to bind to the DNA
evidence_reasoning: This interpretation is inferred from the linear dependence on XPD concentration.

claim: The association rate constant for XPD is konXPD=0.28±0.01s−1nM−1.
source_text: The data were fitted to 1/τ1=konXPD[XPD] yielding the association rate constant konXPD=0.28±0.01s−1nM−1(mean±SD).
evidence_reasoning: This rate constant is determined from fitting the experimental data.

claim: The rate 1/τ2 for first processive unwinding depended on a higher power of the XPD concentration, indicating a requirement for multiple proteins.
source_text: In contrast, the rate 1/τ2 for first processive unwinding depended on a higher power of the XPD concentration (orange squares, Figure 2H), indicating a requirement for multiple proteins.
evidence_reasoning: The higher-order dependence is observed in the data, and the interpretation about multiple proteins is inferred.

claim: The equilibrium dissociation constant for XPD is kd=5nM, similar to that observed in bulk studies.
source_text: The data were fitted to this expression, yielding equilibrium dissociation constant kd=koffXPD/konXPD=5nM (similar to that observed in bulk studies; Pugh et al., 2008a)
evidence_reasoning: The dissociation constant is determined from fitting the data and is consistent with previous bulk measurements.

claim: Low-processivity behavior is due to single-XPD activity, and processive activity from cooperative action of multiple (at minimum, two) monomers.
source_text: The data are consistent with low-processivity behavior being due to single-XPD activity, and processive activity from cooperative action of multiple (at minimum, two) monomers.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is inferred from the concentration dependence experiments and loading site length experiments.

claim: The majority of backsteps measure 1 bp while the less common large backsteps span −4.6 ± 0.9 bp.
source_text: Our step-fitting algorithm reveals that the majority of backsteps measure 1 bp while the less common large backsteps span −4.6 ± 0.9 bp (mean ± SD).
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative measurement from the step-fitting analysis of the data.

claim: Both 1-bp and 5-bp step sizes were independent of ATP.
source_text: In both cases the step sizes were independent of ATP (Figure 4B,C).
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed in the experimental data across different ATP concentrations.

claim: Single-base pair backsteps have so far only been observed in high-resolution optical trap measurements of NS3 helicase, and appear rare.
source_text: Single-base pair backsteps have so far only been observed in high-resolution optical trap measurements of NS3 helicase, and appear rare (Cheng et al., 2011).
evidence_reasoning: This is a statement about previous observations in the literature.

claim: Backsteps are very frequent for XPD.
source_text: In contrast, backsteps are very frequent for XPD.
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in the experimental data showing high frequency of backsteps.

claim: The large 5-bp steps backward and forward exhibited by XPD appear to be a new feature of helicase stepping mechanics that has not been reported before.
source_text: Moreover, the large 5-bp steps backward and forward exhibited by XPD appear to be a new feature of helicase stepping mechanics that, to our knowledge, has not been reported before.
evidence_reasoning: This is a novel observation from the data, with the claim of novelty based on knowledge of the literature.

claim: The probability p− of a 1-bp backstep varied inversely with ATP but remained significant (∼15%) at saturating ATP concentrations.
source_text: p− varied inversely with ATP, but importantly remained significant (∼15%) at saturating ATP concentrations (Figure 4E).
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative observation from the experimental data.

claim: The direction of each 1-bp step was independent of the preceding step.
source_text: We found that probabilities for pairs of adjacent 1-bp steps were simply products of individual probabilities (i.e., the probability for two consecutive backsteps was p−2), indicating that the direction of each 1-bp step was independent of the preceding step.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is inferred from the statistical analysis of step pairs in the data.

claim: 5-bp backsteps were almost always followed by equal-size forward steps (−4.6 vs 4.4 ± 0.9 bp).
source_text: In contrast, the large 5-bp steps displayed a strong correlation to past behavior; 5-bp backsteps were almost always followed by equal-size forward steps (−4.6 vs 4.4 ± 0.9 bp, mean ± SD; [ATP] = 500 μM and F = 12 pN; Table 1).
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative observation from the experimental data.

claim: The pairing of 5-bp backsteps with 5-bp forward steps suggests that XPD kept track of its position along the hairpin after the initial backstep.
source_text: The pairing of 5-bp backsteps with 5-bp forward steps suggests that XPD kept track of its position along the hairpin after the initial backstep.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference based on the observed correlation between backsteps and forward steps.

claim: The probability for 5-bp backsteps p−5 was low (5–10%) and depended weakly on ATP.
source_text: The probability for 5-bp backsteps p−5 was low (5–10%) and depended weakly on ATP.
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative observation from the experimental data.

claim: The frequency of 5-bp steps depends inversely on force.
source_text: Measurements across a range of tensions on alternate hairpin sequences revealed that the frequency of 5-bp steps depends inversely on force (Figure 4—figure supplement 1)
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in experiments varying the applied force.

claim: The dwell times τ between all 1-bp steps exhibited Michaelis-Menten-like behavior.
source_text: As shown in Figure 4F, the dwell times τ between all 1-bp steps (forward or backward) exhibited Michaelis-Menten-like behavior.
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in the experimental data showing the dependence of dwell times on ATP concentration.

claim: Dwell times between 5-bp backsteps and subsequent large forward steps were independent of ATP.
source_text: In contrast, dwell times between 5-bp backsteps and subsequent large forward steps were independent of ATP (Figure 4F).
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed in the experimental data.

claim: Distributions of dwell times between 5-bp backsteps and forward steps were exponential, indicating a single rate-limiting kinetic step.
source_text: Distributions of those dwell times were exponential, indicating a single rate-limiting kinetic step (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence_reasoning: The exponential distribution is observed in the data, and the interpretation about a single rate-limiting step is inferred from kinetic theory.

claim: XPD processivity is highly sequence-dependent.
source_text: XPD processivity is highly sequence-dependent (Figure 5B)
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in experiments with different DNA sequences.

claim: The helicase stalls when the hairpin fork opening probability popen dips below ∼0.1.
source_text: The data indicate that the helicase stalls when popen dips below ∼0.1.
evidence_reasoning: This threshold is determined from correlating processivity with calculated opening probabilities.

claim: Confronted with stable sequences (i.e., when popen is small), the helicase exhibits a higher frequency of backsteps.
source_text: Confronted with stable sequences (i.e., when popen is small), the helicase exhibits a higher frequency of backsteps (Figure 6A).
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in the experimental data correlating backstep probability with sequence stability.

claim: The rate of stepping forward kF is suppressed when popen is small.
source_text: This occurs primarily because the rate of stepping forward kF is suppressed (Figure 6B).
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in the experimental data showing the dependence of forward rate on opening probability.

claim: The linear dependence of kF on popen at saturating ATP suggests a 'passive' unwinding mechanism in which the helicase captures spontaneously opened base pairs.
source_text: The linear dependence of kF on popen at saturating ATP suggests a 'passive' unwinding mechanism in which the helicase captures spontaneously opened base pairs at the ssDNA/dsDNA junction.
evidence_reasoning: The linear dependence is observed in the data, and the mechanistic interpretation is inferred.

claim: A strictly passive model requires that the rate be strictly proportional to popen, whereas the observed linear trend exhibits an offset.
source_text: However, a strictly passive model (Betterton and Jülicher, 2005; Delagoutte and von Hippel, 2002; Johnson et al., 2007; Manosas et al., 2010) requires that the rate be strictly proportional to popen, whereas the observed linear trend exhibits an offset.
evidence_reasoning: The offset is observed in the data, and its significance is interpreted in the context of theoretical models from the literature.

claim: The offset in the linear trend is indicative of an intrinsic destabilization of the duplex by the helicase, characteristic of an 'active' mechanism.
source_text: This feature is indicative of an intrinsic destabilization of the duplex by the helicase, characteristic of an 'active' mechanism
evidence_reasoning: This interpretation is inferred from the observed offset in the data.

claim: The fork is destabilized by 1.9 kBT through interaction with the protein.
source_text: The fork is destabilized by 1.9 kBT through interaction with the protein
evidence_reasoning: This value is determined from fitting the kinetic model to the experimental data.

claim: The fit yields a translocation rate ktrans ≈ 10 nt/s, in excellent agreement with that determined from independent measurements of XPD translocation on ssDNA.
source_text: We highlight the fact that the fit yields a translocation rate ktrans ≈ 10 nt/s (obtained in the limit that popen = 1), in excellent agreement with that determined from independent measurements of XPD translocation on ssDNA (Honda et al., 2009).
evidence_reasoning: The translocation rate is determined from the model fit and is consistent with independent measurements from the literature.

claim: 3′–5′ SF1A helicases must remain in register with DNA because its bases are intercalated between aromatic residues of the active site.
source_text: In contrast to 3′–5′ SF1A helicases, which must remain in register with DNA because its bases are intercalated between aromatic residues of the active site
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about SF1A helicase structure and mechanism from the literature.

claim: 5′–3′ SF2 helicases like XPD do not have base-intercalating residues and instead interact with the DNA phosphodiester backbone.
source_text: In contrast to 3′–5′ SF1A helicases, which must remain in register with DNA because its bases are intercalated between aromatic residues of the active site
evidence_reasoning: This is implied by the contrast drawn with SF1A helicases and is consistent with structural knowledge of SF2 helicases.

claim: Large ∼5-bp backsteps likely involve rearrangements of the translocating DNA strand relative to a secondary binding site.
source_text: Large ∼5-bp backsteps likely involve a different mechanism. Based on structural data, we propose that these events represent rearrangements of the translocating DNA strand relative to a secondary binding site.
evidence_reasoning: This mechanism is proposed based on structural data from the literature and the observed stepping behavior.

claim: Typical SF2 helicases contain a bipartite nucleic acid binding site that accommodates up to 8 nt (or bp) of nucleic acid.
source_text: Whereas typical SF2 helicases contain a bipartite nucleic acid binding site that accommodates up to 8 nt (or bp) of nucleic acid
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about SF2 helicase structure from the literature.

claim: XPD and related 5′–3′, FeS-containing helicases feature additional contacts with the translocating strand beyond the canonical binding site.
source_text: XPD and related 5′–3′, FeS-containing helicases feature additional contacts with the translocating strand beyond this canonical binding site.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on biochemical and structural analyses cited in the manuscript.

claim: The secondary DNA binding site in XPD accommodates ∼5 nt.
source_text: As shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1, this site accommodates ∼5 nt.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from structural analysis of XPD and related helicases.

claim: The observed 5-bp backsteps occur when the translocating strand dissociates from the secondary binding site, allowing the 5 nt normally occluded to re-anneal with the complementary strand.
source_text: We propose that the observed 5-bp backsteps occur when the translocating strand dissociates from this secondary binding site, allowing the 5 nt normally occluded to re-anneal with the complementary strand.
evidence_reasoning: This mechanism is proposed to explain the observed 5-bp backsteps based on structural considerations.

claim: The secondary binding site separates the motor core from the wedge structure that splits the duplex.
source_text: The 5-bp back and forward steps illustrate the importance of the secondary binding site in controlling XPD helicase activity: it separates the motor core from the wedge structure that splits the duplex.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from structural data and the observed stepping behavior.

claim: Unwinding occurs only when the translocating strand resides within the secondary DNA binding site.
source_text: Unwinding occurs only when the translocating strand resides within this secondary DNA binding site.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the proposed mechanism and the observed stepping behavior.

claim: The secondary binding site allows control of 5′–3′ translocation and force generation by XPD.
source_text: This not only allows control of 5′–3′ translocation and force generation by XPD
evidence_reasoning: This functional role is inferred from structural studies cited in the manuscript.

claim: The secondary binding site stalls the helicase at bulky UV-induced damage, thereby triggering nucleotide excision repair.
source_text: but also stalls the helicase at bulky UV-induced damage, thereby triggering nucleotide excision repair
evidence_reasoning: This functional role is supported by cited studies (Mathieu et al., 2010, 2013).

claim: The origin of the low processivity of XPD is the sequence dependence.
source_text: The origin of the low processivity of XPD (Figure 1D) is the sequence dependence.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is inferred from the observed correlation between processivity and sequence-dependent opening probabilities.

claim: When kF and kR are equal, the average unwinding rate is zero.
source_text: When kF and kR are equal, the average unwinding rate is zero.
evidence_reasoning: This is a logical consequence of the kinetic model where forward and reverse rates balance.

claim: The biological function of XPD's inefficient unwinding likely reflects its cellular role, which requires unwinding of short duplex regions.
source_text: The biological function of this inefficient unwinding likely reflects the cellular role of XPD helicase, which requires unwinding of short duplex regions.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative interpretation connecting the observed mechanism to biological function.

claim: The sequence-dependence of XPD's unwinding activity makes XPD suitable for its function in NER and transcription.
source_text: The sequence-dependence of XPD's unwinding activity we report here makes XPD suitable for its function in NER and transcription.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative interpretation of the functional significance of the observed sequence dependence.

claim: Having a highly processive and vigorous helicase uncoupled from its respective macromolecular machinery would be undesirable for the cell.
source_text: Having a highly processive and vigorous helicase uncoupled from its respective macromolecular machinery (such as TFIIH complex in the case of XPD) would be undesirable for the cell.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative statement about cellular regulation and function.

claim: Protein partners may play an important role in facilitating and regulating XPD helicase unwinding activity.
source_text: Protein partners may play an important role in facilitating and regulating XPD helicase unwinding activity
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative statement supported by previous work (Pugh et al., 2008b).

claim: The conserved domain architecture of all SF2B helicases predicts that these helicases will share a common unwinding mechanism with XPD.
source_text: The conserved domain architecture of all SF2B helicases (including human FANCJ, RTEL and CHLR1; White, 2009) predicts that these helicases will share a common unwinding mechanism with XPD, despite a broad range of cellular functions.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative prediction based on structural conservation across the SF2B family.

claim: Distinct protein partners play a role in defining helicase role.
source_text: We thus speculate that distinct protein partners play a role in defining helicase role.
evidence_reasoning: This is explicitly stated as speculation about how helicase function is regulated.

claim: XPD has functions outside of the TFIIH complex.
source_text: It is known that XPD has functions outside of the TFIIH complex
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge from the literature.

claim: By associating with different partners, XPD can play a role in chromosome segregation.
source_text: by associating with different partners, XPD can play a role in chromosome segregation (Ito et al., 2010)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by cited work (Ito et al., 2010).

claim: By associating with different partners, XPD can play a role in the cell's defense against retroviral infection.
source_text: and in the cell's defense against retroviral infection (Yoder et al., 2006)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by cited work (Yoder et al., 2006).

claim: The basic mechanistic features underlying duplex unwinding by SF2B helicases are likely to be conserved for all SF2B enzymes.
source_text: The basic mechanistic features underlying duplex unwinding by these helicases are likely to be conserved for all SF2B enzymes
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative statement based on the conserved architecture of SF2B helicases.
